items.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine has right to defend itself after Trump calls latest strikes a 'disgrace'
items.blurb: EU leaders rally around Ukraine's president after new criticism from Donald Trump, who says Zelensky is "more difficult to work with than Putin".
items.text: President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he is "only standing up for Ukraine's interests" after scathing criticism from Donald Trump, who said Kyiv's new wave of strikes on Russian oil refineries was a "disgrace". The US president, who recently made a controversial deal with Moscow to import diesel, also said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with than Russian President Vladimir Putin". Zelensky, who has been angered by the diesel deal, said he could not accept it, because a gas agreement could come next. "If I don't stand up to this... who else will?" he said at an EU summit in Brussels. Tensions between Washington and Kyiv have escalated over the diesel deal and curbs on Ukraine's battlefield satellite network. Zelensky's trip to Brussels, following a visit to London, has come at the end of a bruising week. As he arrived at the summit on Friday, where EU leaders rallied around him in support, Zelensky said it was good to be back among allies. items.headline: Qatar announces ‘massive’ solar plant project in Lebanon
items.blurb: Sheikh Mohammed also discussed Israeli 'violations' in Lebanese territory with Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.
items.text: Qatar’s prime minister has announced plans to set up what he described as a “massive” solar plant in Lebanon to help ease its energy crisis . Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani made the announcement during his visit to Beirut on Friday, after meeting his Lebanese counterpart, Nawaf Salam. “We have agreed to establish a comprehensive framework for cooperation in the energy sector and to present viable solutions,” Sheikh Mohammed said. QatarEnergy has reached an agreement with French company TotalEnergies to jointly develop a solar power plant in Lebanon as an initial project. The aim is to develop a major investment project “that would benefit the Lebanese economy, as well as the Qatari companies and entities participating in it”, he added. Prime Minister Salam said he would put the plans for Lebanon’s electricity sector to the Lebanese Cabinet soon. “The Qatari side will fund, implement and activate the project without any cost on the Lebanese state,” Lebanon’s leader said, adding that such a move is important because of the country’s financial crisis. items.headline: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
items.blurb: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report .
items.text: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report . More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network , an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status. The intensifying crackdown comes as the law criminalising homosexuality in the country was toughened earlier this year. On 11 March, Senegal’s parliament amended the penal code, doubling the maximum prison term for consensual same-sex relations to 10 years. The new law introduced penalties of up to seven years in prison and a fine of 500,000 to 5m CFA francs (£650–£6,500) for promoting homosexuality, or supporting or financing LGBTQ+ people and organisations. items.headline: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
items.blurb: The BBC sees masked settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest olives, amid a surge in similar incidents.
items.text: Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt. Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence : a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby. The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car. "We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys … started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head and my neck – look, I am bleeding!" items.headline: How Israeli firm’s ‘zero-click’ malware attack poses global security risk
items.blurb: A new ‘zero-click’ hack uses ads to target victims without any action needed on their part.
items.text: Just visiting a page or refreshing an app can be enough to fall victim to a malware attack in which your personal data is stolen from a laptop or phone, researchers have found. You are not even required to “click” on anything. An Israeli spyware firm has been found to be behind the first-known instance of “zero-click” targeted advertising in which fraudsters or spies can steal private data and send it to external servers, with Al Jazeera journalists among the victims. In June 2025, 45 devices used by Al Jazeera staff – including several who reported on sensitive subjects – were targeted with spyware which installed itself without the need to open or download any files. An investigation by the Canada-based academic research unit Citizen Lab, prompted by Al Jazeera’s initial internal probe into the issue, discovered that the Israeli company Candiru was behind the attacks. items.blurb: Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.
items.text: Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.” Vara said that she had run the story through the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, and it had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated. The exception, she said, was an epigraph from what is described as an unpublished poem by the South African writer Vangile Gantsho. items.headline: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis
items.blurb: The pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after having surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday.
items.text: Pope Leo XIV has been pictured celebrating Mass from hospital, in the first images of him released by the Vatican since he underwent lung surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications. The images shared on Friday showed the Chicago-born Pope wearing a green robe while standing behind a makeshift altar on the tenth floor of the hospital. Pope Leo "celebrated with the medical and nursing staff" and thanked workers for their service, the Vatican press office said. On Friday, the Pope's doctors said tests had shown "a steady improvement in his general condition" since his procedure. His doctors said that a chest X-ray indicated "good recovery of the operated lung". The whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical", the Vatican said following the surgery. The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr , secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist. items.headline: Dad fined after son, 2, died in Cyprus hotel fall
items.blurb: Joshua Foster "lost control" of his son while showing him the view of a water park from a window.
items.text: A father whose two-year-old boy fell from a fourth floor window of a Cyprus hotel has been fined €3,000 (£2,500) for causing his death. Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed his son on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and "lost control" of him , Paphos District Court previously heard. The toddler fell nearly 40ft (12.1m) at the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort on 12 July, the first day of the family's holiday in Chlorakas. Foster, 37, from Essex, admitted causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act and was sentenced earlier. He told reporters afterwards: "Thank you for the support. I'm looking forward to going home and being with my wife and daughter." Later, the family said in a statement: "We are relieved that this process is now over, but for our family, the consequences of this tragedy will never end. "Our son was deeply loved and will be forever missed. His loss is something we carry with us every day." Foster, an auditor, arrived in Cyprus hours

items.blurb: A protest rally was organised under the leadership of the Thiruvananthapuram Bar Association at the Vanchiyoor Court complex
items.text: Lawyers boycotted courts across Thiruvananthapuram district on Friday in protest against the City Police’s “failure” to suspend a traffic police officer, who allegedly assaulted K.P. Jayachandran, former Additional Advocate General and State president of the Indian Association of Lawyers. Mr. Jayachandran, a former president of the Thiruvananthapuram Bar Association and a present member of the Kerala Bar Council, was allegedly assaulted by a senior civil police officer attached to the Thiruvananthapuram City Traffic Police near the Kerala Administrative Tribunal in Vanchiyoor on Thursday. In his complaint, the lawyer claimed that the police officer was taking photos of all vehicles parked on the road side. When Mr. Jayachandran questioned the reason behind his action, the police officer purportedly assaulted him and hurled abuses at him. However, the Vanchiyoor police maintained that there was no wrongdoing on the officer’s part. Nonetheless, the complaint was being examined. A case was yet to be registered, an official said. items.headline: Chaos at Chhattisgarh garba event as right-wing workers create ruckus over presence of Muslims
items.blurb: A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was reportedly pushed.
items.text: A garba event organised in Chhattisgarh's Durg descended into chaos on Wednesday after workers of right-wing groups reportedly created ruckus over the presence of Muslim youth at the event. A scuffle broke out on the stage during which Congress district president and former mayor Dheeraj Bakliwal was pushed, the Times of India reported. The videos of the incident were shared on social media that showed the right-wing workers on the stage raising objection over the presence of Muslim youth at the event. According to reports, the dispute reportedly began after an NSUI office-bearer identified as Adil Khan shared a poster of the event on social media with details of the event and mentioning free entry passes. On Wednesday night when the garba event was underway, members of right wing outfits, Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), reached the venue and barged on the stage. items.headline: Krishna Byre Gowda sets October 31 deadline for replacement of streetlights
items.text: A file photo of Krishna Byre Gowda | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J. Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has set October 31 as the deadline for completing the installation and replacement of LED streetlights across Bengaluru. On Friday, Mr. Gowda held a virtual meeting and directed officials to physically inspect streetlights after installation and verify their functioning instead of relying solely on reports of completed work. Contractors would be penalised if lights were not installed properly or failed to function, he said. He directed the officials to intensify field inspections and penalise contractors for maintenance failures. The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has so far imposed fines totalling ₹93.67 lakh on contractors for failing to maintain streetlights. He told the officials to replace sodium-vapour streetlights with LED lights in the East City Corporation jurisdiction. In a press statement, the Minister’s office said that the directions were issued after three months of reviews of streetlight installation and maintenance. items.headline: Sudhakar Dalela appointed next Indian Ambassador to Nepal
items.text: Sudhakar Dalela, presently Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs, has been appointed as India’s next envoy to Nepal. Dalela will succeed Naveen Srivastava, who recently completed his three-year term. A day earlier, Nepal had cleared the name of Nischal Nath Pandey as the ambassador to India. The appointments come in the wake of New Delhi and Kathmandu engaging to work out the first bilateral visit of Prime Minister Balen Shah to India next month. The appointment of a secretary-level officer to Kathmandu is also a step up from previous practice, where India typically dispatched Additional Secretary-rank officials to Kathmandu, signaling elevated importance given to the bilateral relationship in the neighborhood. Announcing Dalela’s appointment on Friday evening, the Ministry of External Affairs said that Dalela is expected to take up the assignment shortly. An expert on India’s engagement with South Asia, Dalela most recently served as India’s ambassador to Bhutan between 2022 and 2025. In September last year, he was appointed as Secretary, Economic Relations, handling India’s economic diplomacy; development partnership with countries in the Global South, multilateral economic relations.

items.headline: India rejects US lawmaker Pramila Jayapal’s remarks on voter roll revision as ‘unwarranted’
items.blurb: India rejected US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s criticism of the voter roll revision, calling her remarks “unwarranted and uninformed” and interference in electoral practices.
items.text: India on Friday rejected senior US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal s criticism of the revision of the country’s electoral rolls as unwarranted and tantamount to interfering in the “electoral practices of a fellow democracy”. Jayapal, an Indian-origin lawmaker from the Democratic Party who has been a vocal critic of the Indian government, said on social media on Thursday that she was concerned about actions that appeared aimed at purging 130 million people from voting rolls. When external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked about the matter at a regular media briefing, he replied: “We find the remarks of the Congresswoman unwarranted and uninformed and tantamount to interfering in the electoral practices of a fellow democracy.” Jayapal, who was born in Chennai and moved to the US in 1982, said on social media that she was “deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls”. The move “appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing in the US to undermine voting rights in a democracy”, she said.

items.headline: Bengaluru space-tech firm The Guild unveils 150-acre rocket testing facility near Sriharikota
items.blurb: Ethereal Exploration Guild’s new facility will support development of its fully reusable medium-lift launch vehicle.
items.text: A view of The Guild's rocket development and testing facility set up in Tirupati district BY ARRANGEMENT | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT Ethereal Exploration Guild (The Guild), a Bengaluru-based private space technology company, on Friday unveiled The Anchorage, a 150-acre rocket development and testing facility in Space City, about 40 km from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) at Sriharikota in Tirupati district. The facility will provide ground infrastructure for the development and testing of Razor Crest Mk 1 (RCM1), the company’s fully reusable medium-lift launch vehicle, according to a press release issued by the company. The RCM1 is being designed for the recovery and reuse of both its booster and upper stage. Its propulsion architecture comprises two semi-cryogenic rocket engines: Pegasus, an 80 kN upper-stage engine designed to power the reusable upper stage, and Stallion, a 1.2 MN gas-generator booster engine intended for lift-off and atmospheric ascent. Pegasus incorporates the company’s Full-Flow Segregated Cooling Cycle (FSCC) and a dual-thrust-chamber architecture. items.headline: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget
items.blurb: Senior banking executives have told the BBC they expect to be "on the menu" in the chancellor's Budget tax later this month.
items.text: Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC. Healey has described banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, but leaders in the sector have said it will be "on the menu" at the Budget in two weeks' time. The biggest four banks collectively made about £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, and trade unions have called for them to face additional taxes. The trade body for the banking sector, UK Finance, warned "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode". Shares in banks including Lloyds and NatWest fell on Friday on expectations that the sector would be hit by tax hikes. The firms were among the biggest fallers on the UK stock market, with both dropping more than 2%. Barclays fell only slightly and HSBC actually rose as both have large international businesses and would be less affected by a hike in UK taxes.

items.headline: Chandrasekaran, P.B. Balaji to join Iveco board as Tata deal reaches final stage
items.blurb: While N. Chandrasekaran will join as Iveco’s chairperson, P.B. Balaji and Girish Wagh Wagh will join as non-independent directors.
items.text: New Delhi: Tata Sons' chairperson Natarajan Chandrasekaran, Jaguar Land Rover's chief executive P.B. Balaji, and Tata Motors' managing director Girish Wagh are among the top executives set to join Iveco’s board if Tata Motors’ acquisition of the Italian truckmaker clears its final hurdles. The deal was approved by Iveco shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Friday, with attention now turning to Tata securing 80% acceptance of the tender offer by 26 October. The appointments are conditional on the deal going through. While Chandrasekaran will join as Iveco’s chairperson, Balaji and Wagh will join as non-independent directors. items.headline: Enterprise AI's real risk isn't autonomous agents. It's the complexity between them.
items.blurb: Presented by Gravitee
items.text: Agent complexity is the insidious shadow lurking inside enterprises right now that needs a light shone on it. That’s because enterprises don't deploy a single agent and watch it run, they deploy fleets, each one calling APIs, calling other agents, reaching into applications that were never built with a machine decision-maker in mind. That's the failure mode that should keep you up at night: a windy, complicated system nobody can see clearly enough to govern. But why do things get so opaque so quickly? Add a second agent to a system, and you've added one connection. Add a tenth, and you haven't added ten connections, you've potentially added dozens, because now any agent might call any other, and each of those calls can trigger a call somewhere else. Complexity doesn't creep up with agent headcount. It compounds with the number of paths between agents, and nobody's job is to draw that graph. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says. The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. items.headline: When agents act on their own, governance has to live in the data layer
items.blurb: Presented by EDB
items.text: As enterprises give AI agents more autonomy — the ability to plan, decide, and act across systems without a human approving each step — a hard question moves to the center of every architecture review: When an agent tries to complete an action that it was never authorized to do, what actually stops it? These are your agents, running on your models, touching your data in your infrastructure — and the responsibility for what they do sits with you. That responsibility can’t be met in hindsight or with a set of abstract policies that live on paper but not in practice. Agents need rules in the context of the moment, because they don’t exercise overriding judgment of their own actions. Consider a simple rule: Never open the car door. Followed literally, an agent could never get in or out of the car at all.
